items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I learned that she had been among the young girls that went to the house on Hathaway Street when Dolly and Dyer Jones went there to rehearse

ctx.x: Many people stood in front of the band stand and watched the musicians and listened to the music. Some never danced and I was one that never danced when I went to hear an orchestra. I knew that this girl liked to dance but all that she did that night was to stand in front of the band and look at me. I knew that Edgar James expected me to act as a young man should after he had told me this girl was watching me.

At the next intermission, I asked the girl to have a drink with me and she accepted. Alcohol wasn't sold in dance halls so we had some kind of soft drink and talked until I went back on the band stand. I did not ask her for a date until I had talked to her at a few other dances. It then started to get serious and we were together quite often. Her name was Madelyn Grant and as time went on, I learned that she had been among the young girls that went to the house on Hathaway Street when Dolly and Dyer Jones went…

Madelyn was a tall brown-skinned girl, not fat but strongly built with large eyes. She and I were about the same height, me being perhaps 2 inches taller than she. She was one year older than myself and had come to Cincinnati from Birmingham, Alabama, with an aunt, as both of her parents were dead when I met her. I don't believe I was seriously in love with her,
